title: From Regulation to Engineering: Organizational Privacy Climate as Mediator
abstract: arXiv:2610.32576v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Data protection legislation aims to protect privacy rights by regulating how information systems store and process personal information. While such legislation defines legal obligations, translating regulatory requirements into engineering practice is far from straightforward. As new frameworks such as the EU AI Act emerge, understanding these mechanisms becomes increasingly relevant. To investigate them, we conducted an online survey of 156 U.S. information system developers, examining the role of organizational privacy climate in the association between developers' perceptions of the GDPR and their privacy engineering practices. Using structural equation modeling, we found that organizational privacy climate mediates the relation between developers' perceived GDPR importance and their privacy attitudes, which in turn are associated with their privacy engineering practices. translated_title: 从法规到工程实践：组织隐私氛围的中介作用
translated_abstract: 数据保护立法旨在通过规范信息系统存储和处理个人信息的方式来保护隐私权。虽然此类立法界定了法律义务，但将监管要求转化为工程实践远非易事。随着欧盟《人工智能法案》等新框架的出现，理解这些机制变得日益重要。为研究这些机制，我们对156名美国信息系统开发者进行了在线调查，考察了组织隐私氛围在开发者对GDPR的认知与其隐私工程实践之间关联中所扮演的角色。通过结构方程建模，我们发现组织隐私氛围在开发者感知的GDPR重要性与他们的隐私态度之间起中介作用，而这些隐私态度又与他们的隐私工程实践相关联。这一中介链条——法规、氛围、态度、实践——揭示了监管要求如何转化为实际工程实践。
tldr: 该研究通过对156名美国信息系统开发者的调查发现，组织隐私氛围是连接法规与实践的关键中介——开发者对GDPR重要性的认知通过塑造组织隐私氛围影响其隐私态度，进而驱动其隐私工程实践。
en_tdlr: Surveying 156 U.S. information system developers, this study reveals that organizational privacy climate serves as a key mediator, whereby developers' perceptions of GDPR importance shape their privacy attitudes and ultimately drive their privacy engineering practices.
